title: Tanshinone IIA attenuates cerebral-ischemia-reperfusion-induced neuroinflammation by inhibiting the TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling cascade: A study integrating network pharmacology, bioinformatics, and experimental validation.
authors: Zhou, Chenxi; Yu, Zhexuan; Chen, Tianxue; Chen, Qianqian; Zhang, Yangyang; Cai, Jiawei; Xu, Cenglin; Yu, Li
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丹参酮IIA通过TLR4/NF-kB通路减轻脑缺血再灌注炎症，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tanshinone IIA is the primary compound of Salvia miltiorrhiza, has neuroprotective and antioxidant properties. However, its anti-inflammatory role in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury is not well understood. PURPOSE: To determine whether Tanshinone IIA alleviates inflammation in CIRI via the TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. METHODS: Bioinformatics and network pharmacology analysis revealedCIRI-related targets of Tanshinone IIA. Furthermore, CytoHubba was employed to assess the Protein-protein interaction networks and hub targets. Moreover, molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations assessed Tanshinone IIA binding to core proteins. For in vivo, an MCAO/R rat model, and in vitro, OGD/R-injured HUVECs were used to evaluate neurological function, infarct size, histopathology (TTC, HE, TUNEL), cytokine levels (ELISA), and molecular markers (RT-qPCR, Western blot). RESULTS: The data revealed 10 hub targets including TLR4 and NFKB1, which were enriched in inflammatory pathways such as the "Toll-like receptor signaling pathway" and "NF-kappaB signaling pathway". Furthermore, it was observed that Tanshinone IIA stably interacted with TLR4/NFKB1 (binding energy < -5 kcal/mol) and maintained structural stability in MD simulations. In vivo, Tanshinone IIA improved neurological outcomes, reduced infarct volume, and suppressed IL-1beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha expression, while also downregulating TLR4 and MyD88 expression, inhibiting NF-kappaB p65 phosphorylation, and preventing IkappaB degradation (p < 0.05). In vitro, it attenuated OGD/R-induced apoptosis and TLR4/NF-kappaB activation by reducing TLR4 and MyD88 expression, suppressing NF-kappaB p65 phosphorylation, and stabilizing IkappaB (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: This study revealed that Tanshinone IIA exert anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by targeting the TLR4/NF-kappaB pathway, supporting its therapeutic potential.
abstract_zh: 背景：丹参酮IIA是丹参的主要活性成分，具有神经保护和抗氧化特性。然而，其在脑缺血再灌注损伤中的抗炎作用尚未充分阐明。目的：探讨丹参酮IIA是否通过TLR4/NF-kappaB信号通路减轻脑缺血再灌注损伤中的炎症反应。方法：通过生物信息学和网络药理学分析揭示丹参酮IIA的脑缺血再灌注损伤相关靶点。进一步采用CytoHubba评估蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络及核心靶点。此外，利用分子对接和100 ns分子动力学模拟评估丹参酮IIA与核心蛋白的结合情况。在体内实验中，采用MCAO/R大鼠模型；在体外实验中，使用OGD/R损伤的HUVECs，评估神经功能、梗死面积、组织病理学（TTC、HE、TUNEL）、细胞因子水平（ELISA）及分子标志物（RT-qPCR、Western blot）。结果：数据揭示10个核心靶点，包括TLR4和NFKB1，这些靶点富集于炎症通路，如“Toll样受体信号通路”和“NF-kappaB信号通路”。此外，观察到丹参酮IIA与TLR4/NFKB1稳定结合（结合能 < -5 kcal/mol），并在分子动力学模拟中保持结构稳定性。在体内实验中，丹参酮IIA改善神经功能结局、减少梗死体积，并抑制IL-1beta、IL-6和TNF-alpha表达，同时下调TLR4和MyD88表达、抑制NF-kappaB p65磷酸化，并阻止IkappaB降解（p < 0.05）。在体外实验中，它通过减少TLR4和MyD88表达、抑制NF-kappaB p65磷酸化及稳定IkappaB，减轻OGD/R诱导的细胞凋亡和TLR4/NF-kappaB激活（p < 0.05）。结论：本研究揭示丹参酮IIA通过靶向TLR4/NF-kappaB通路在脑缺血再灌注损伤中发挥抗炎和神经保护作用，支持其治疗潜力。
